Clouds are large masses of water vapor or ice that float in the atmosphere and form when warm air rises and cools, condensing into tiny droplets. These droplets grow larger as they collide with other particles in the air, forming clouds. When conditions are right, such as high pressure systems bringing moisture from the ground, rain can fall from the sky. Clouds play important roles in weather patterns around the world, affecting everything from temperature to precipitation.
